_comment: Triage of every accelerator-mapping avenue for the SmolVLA experts, by impact and feasibility. Status is evidence-backed: 'done' requires a measurement or a tool output, not an argument.

baseline.note: measured CPU cells; DSP and HTA excluded pre-rewrite

avenues.evidence: 64->0 prefill, 48->0 decode; bit-exact on all 33/1 outputs; tiles 115->36 / 101->39

Sin/Cos constant-folded (rotary depends only on position_ids). prefill 2->0, decode 4->0; bit-exact at the folded position sequence. Found empirically: DSP ElementWiseUnary rejects Param[0]=14 (Sin opcode) -- no slicing could fix it.

SOLVED. SNPE input lists take FLOAT32 raws regardless of the network's internal dtype. attention_mask written as uint8 (12769 B) was exactly 1/4 the expected float32 extent (51076 B), which the tool reported as 'batch size 4' rather than a dtype error. With float32 raws: 'Quantization completed successfully', prefill_nomask_q.dlc 157.9 MB (from 629.7 MB fp32).
int8 path works; fp16 not needed
ONNX already static [1,...]; the phantom batch was a float32-raw convention issue, not a batch issue
Whole-graph single tile is impossible: exactly ONE fused RmsNorm (op 1189 of 1190, producing vlm_output_embeds) has no DSP implementation.

Cut before the final RmsNorm. The 1108-op trunk CONVERTS, QUANTIZES and COMPOSES on DSP: ctx_trunk_dsp.bin, 158,467,168 bytes. This is the first time any SmolVLA expert has produced a working accelerator context.
DSP rejects a BOOL_8 graph input (0x508 = QNN_DATATYPE_BOOL_8, Input[0]). Retyped; bit-exact. No op-level fix could address this -- the rejection is on the input tensor.

avenues.what: prevent RmsNorm fusion (op package missing on v66 DSP)
avenues.evidence: Mul-by-1.0 barriers after all 33 ReduceMean did NOT defeat the converter's matcher -- RmsNorm still emitted. No RmsNorm pass exists in --dump_ir_optimizer_config_template, so it cannot be disabled by config. No op package ships for it: libQnnDspV66Skel.so has no RmsNorm, and there are no registerable oppackage .so files in the SDK or on the board. Fusion happens at CONVERT time so switching to HTA would not help.

avenues.what: float32 raws for all inputs regardless of network dtype
avenues.evidence: SNPE input lists take float32 raws. attention_mask as uint8 was exactly 1/4 the float32 extent, reported as a phantom 'batch size 4'. Also: vlm_embeds is [1,960,113] (axes-to-spatial-first-order) and position_ids is Int_32 (keep_int64_inputs=False).

EXECUTED on a freshly booted board. status ok, graph 'trunk', 3 iters: init 1032.4 ms, median execute 1384.5 ms (min 1383.3, max 1384.6, std 0.6 ms -- very stable). The earlier wedge was memory pressure from a prior run, not a hard limit.

avenues.what: compose the trunk on HTA instead of DSP
avenues.evidence: ComposeGraphs Failed with error = 1. HTA is far more restricted than DSP and the trunk is MatMul/FullyConnected-heavy rather than convolutional. DSP is the only accelerator that takes this graph.

verdict.op_support: SOLVED -- 0 of 1197 ops lack DSP/HTA support after R1-R4
verdict.composition: SOLVED for the 1108-op trunk (S2); blocked only by one un-implementable fused RmsNorm at the tail
verdict.execution: DONE -- 1384.5 ms median on DSP, init 1032.4 ms
verdict.tiles_required: 2 (DSP trunk + CPU RmsNorm tail), far inside the ~56 ceiling
verdict.performance: NEGATIVE. DSP 1384.5 ms vs CPU 583.8 ms = 2.37x SLOWER. The full rewrite chain successfully maps the expert prefill onto the DSP, and the mapping is not worth taking. Consistent with the vision result, where DSP was slowest on every one of 49 segments (3609.6 ms serial vs CPU 3172.2). Hexagon v66 is not competitive with the Kryo 585 for transformer-shaped work on this board.
verdict.backends_tried: CPU (baseline, fastest), DSP (composes+executes, 2.37x slower), HTA (does not compose)
verdict.exhausted: YES. Rewrites R1-R5, dtype D1-D3, calibration C1, slicing S1-S2, runtime X1 and backend A1 all carry evidence-backed verdicts. The expert prefill IS mappable to the DSP; the mapping is measurably not worth taking.
